subject: Sum by group (stan equivalent of R's tapply)

messages.author: 3879f7125955e3e9
messages.subject: Sum by group (stan equivalent of R's tapply)
parts:
Stan users:

What is the best way of summing a set of values by group, like the function tapply in R

For example, if you have the following data

Group  Number
A        10
A        20
B        10
B         5

I want to get the result
A=30
B=15

Or in r code, i am looking for a function that does this
tapply(Number, Group, sum)

For reference:
My application is an attempt at a multinomial logit (still draft stage, only for illustration). See the area where I need help in bold (written in r code now to illustrate what I am trying to accomplish)

data {
    // dimensions and indexed
    int N; // number of observations
    int K; // number of choices
    int P; // number of parameters
    int I; // number of rows
    int observation[I]; // index of observations

    // choices and model matrix
    vector[I] y; // observed choices
    matrix[I,P] X;
  }
parameters {
    vector[P] beta;
  }
model {
    // declare temporary variables
    vector[I] EV; // exponentiated utilities per choice
    vector[I] sumEV; // sum of exp utilities per choice
    vector[I] p; // probabilities per choice

    // calculate probability per observation
    EV <- X*beta;
    sumEV <- tapply(EV, observation, sum)
    sumEV <- rep(sumEV, K)
    p <- EV/sumEV;

    // sum log likelihood
    increment_log_prob(log(p*y));
  }

Thanks a lot!

Best,
Anders

messages.subject: Re: Sum by group (stan equivalent of R's tapply)
parts:
On Friday, January 16, 2015 at 7:24:11 PM UTC-5, Anders Holden wrote:
What is the best way of summing a set of values by group, like the function tapply in R

There isn't a good way. The least bad way is to pass an integer vector or starting indices and group sizes and then use segment(). Like

for(g in 1:groups) sumEV[g] <- sum(segment(EV, starts[g], sizes[g]));

This presumes the observations are sorted by group.

Ben
